name: prof-f09-p-g — extracted from f09-p-g
palette: Muted blues and greys for night and interiors, shifting into warm creams and yellows at breakfast, then more saturated primaries (yellows, reds, turquoise) in play and sports scenes.
light_logic: Naturalistic progression from dim, bluish night light to soft morning interiors, then bright daylight exteriors and evenly lit sports facilities, always motivated by believable sources like windows and ambient daylight.
lens: Mostly medium and wide lenses that keep children in their environments, with occasional closer shots for emphasis but no extreme distortion; perspective stays human and observational.
texture: Soft, lived-in domestic textures (blankets, wallpaper, laundry, concrete alleys) contrasted with clean, slightly glossy sports surfaces (pool water, gym equipment, leotards).
world: Realistic, slightly idealized working- to middle-class urban neighborhood where homes, alleys, and public sports facilities form one continuous, coherent world centered on children’s daily lives.
forbidden: Overly glossy, hyper-stylized lighting that breaks the natural morning-to-day progression
Abstract graphics or heavy VFX that detach the story from real spaces
Harsh conflict or scolding tones that would make the wake-up feel punitive
Fragmented, music-video-style cutting that obscures the sense of a single day unfolding
